source_review.notes: Retrieved and reviewed the Starburst query-rewrite paper record, Cascades paper, current Apache Calcite algebra/adapter documentation, PostgreSQL 18 volatility, expression evaluation, planning, and rule-system documentation, PostgreSQL 18.2 defect notes, current DuckDB internals documentation, and current DuckDB optimizer source. Checked rule equivalence versus cost selection, memoized/heuristic planning, volatility/evaluation-order limits, self-join and constraint planning, rewrite-system terminology, optimizer phases, and the cited unsafe volatile/set-returning pushdown defect.

evidence: Checked D, C, Obs_C, equivalence, substitution theta, L/R/G, redex, normal form, termination, confluence, memo, trait, null rejection, and rule-fuel definitions.
Checked rule soundness is universally quantified over well-typed substitutions and legal database states under an explicit observation contract.
Checked semantic equivalence remains separate from profitability, search completion, normal form, and global optimality.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Schema, type, collation, names/ordinals, nullability, bag multiplicity, order, errors, effects, authorization, snapshot, and physical properties are kept distinct.

evidence: Recomputed four input bag occurrences and the two retained occurrences for nested versus combined selection.
Recomputed projection multiplicities, two inner-join matches, and DISTINCT multiplicity mismatch.
Recomputed left-join pushdown counterexample and the 100 times three equals 300 aggregate amplification example.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Detailed independent finite-bag arithmetic is retained in artifacts/reviews/DBE-061/independent-recomputation.txt.

evidence: Reviewed the selection-cascade proof by per-occurrence TRUE retention under pure total predicates.
Reviewed projection fusion as function composition with bag multiplicity and dependency premises.
Reviewed inner-join alternative proof, outer-join null-extension counterexample, constraint premises, termination measures, and required-property preservation.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Local replacement is explicitly conditioned on congruent enclosing contexts; hidden sequence, effect, security, or policy contexts are not assumed congruent.

evidence: Reviewed empty bags, duplicates, null keys/values, TRUE/FALSE/UNKNOWN, multiple and absent join matches, and guard-false cases.
Reviewed outer/semi/anti/mark/lateral joins, DISTINCT, aggregation, windows, order, limit, recursion, correlated scope, casts, collation, overflow, and throwing/volatile/set-returning functions.

Reviewed unvalidated, informational, deferred, partial, remote, and snapshot-invalid constraints; row security, masking, tenant boundaries, capability mismatch, oscillation, memo explosion, timeout, and fallback.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The finite executable deliberately does not model the full SQL or platform observation contract.

evidence: Checked every rule requires typed bindings, guarded substitution, schema/bag/null/effect/policy preservation, and stable diagnostics.
Checked canonical phases require a decreasing measure or idempotent orientation, while exploration requires memo novelty and resource budgets.
Checked root alternatives deliver required ordering, distribution, convention, and other physical properties before selection.
invariant_checking.notes: Constraint and source-capability metadata are semantic premises only when enforcement, validity, version, and query scope justify reliance.

evidence: Reviewed the formal guarded-rule obligation and the separation of extensional values from other observable behavior.
Reviewed tuple-occurrence proofs for filter combination, projection composition, inner-join alternatives, and the failure of ordinary laws under null extension.
Reviewed system-level termination/confluence distinctions and why individual rule termination does not prove strategy termination.
proof_review.notes: Proof obligations are scoped to an explicit semantic model; implementation and target-engine validation remain separate evidence.

evidence: The executable is labeled a finite model rather than a SQL implementation or proof.
Selection, projection, join, constraint, termination, and property arguments state their assumptions and failure boundaries.
Architecture descriptions from Starburst, Cascades, Calcite, PostgreSQL, and DuckDB are attributed and not generalized into universal guarantees.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Equivalence, theorem assumptions, optimizer policy, heuristic search, and empirical production claims are labeled separately.

evidence: Repository verification passed one standard-library Python snippet with exact nine-line stdout, empty stderr, zero exit status, and recorded Python 3.14.4 toolchain.
Independent recomputation reproduced selection/projection/join laws, duplicate and outer-join counterexamples, and aggregate multiplication.
All eleven source artifacts were retained under artifacts/references/DBE-061 and repository-local links were checked by validation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live SQL engine comparison, optimizer build, rule injection, randomized SQL fuzzer, remote pushdown, security policy, production query, planning benchmark, or canary was executed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed progression from observation contract and guarded rule through bound representation, selection/projection/join/aggregate/constant/constraint semantics, security boundaries, rewrite strategies, termination, memo search, layered validation, observability, and release. Meaning preservation, search generation, cost choice, and operations remain distinct.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed a production rule lifecycle with stable rule identity, proof/side conditions, typed bindings, capability and policy boundaries, phase/memo ownership, time/memory/match budgets, privacy-safe traces, semantic and planning regressions, canary cohorts, kill switches, minimized counterexamples, and rollback.

pedagogical_review.notes: The chapter begins from observational equivalence, derives guarded rewrite obligations, implements a finite bag model, contrasts valid laws with counterexamples, covers fourteen failure modes, provides ten distinct worked examples, and progresses five exercises from rule definition to an elite multitenant release gate with complete answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, official/primary-source, mathematical, executable-snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external database optimizer maintainer, query-processing researcher, SQL standards expert, language-semantics reviewer, extension author, security/privacy specialist, distributed-source owner, reliability engineer, or independent educator review is claimed. The chapter and finite model prove neither full SQL equivalence, soundness of any production optimizer rule, correctness of third-party metadata/functions/constraints, semantics of remote engines, termination or optimality of arbitrary rule systems, representative planning/execution performance, policy compliance, certification, nor deployment fitness.
